sources.name: HMRC estimated cost of tax reliefs, January 2026

aggregate.label: Estimated cost of non-structural reliefs with available multi-year estimates
aggregate.rounding: Official aggregate rounded to £1 billion; independently costed reliefs are not an abolition revenue estimate.

notes: Tax relief cost ≠ revenue available. Estimates do not model all behavioural responses, interactions or wider economic effects of abolition.
Do not add relief costs to government expenditure, borrowing or PSNB.
The official headline excludes single-year estimates, withheld estimates and uncosted reliefs. Coverage varies by year.
2025-26 is predominantly forecast. Individual first-forecast years are retained; earlier values are estimates, not necessarily final outturn.
Negligible means less than £3 million; shown as missing numeric values, never zero.
HMRC tax heads and structural/non-structural classifications are retained verbatim apart from letter case. Multiple-tax-head amounts must not be duplicated across tax-head totals.
Description is HMRC’s description of a relief; no inferred policy objective is supplied.

reliefs.name: Business Asset Disposal Relief
reliefs.description: Certain disposals chargeable to CGT by individuals and qualifying trustees of all or part of a business are charged at 10% for gains up to April 2025, 14% for gains between April 2025 and April 2026 and 18% thereafter. Qualifying gains for each individual are subject to a £1 million lifetime limit. The relief is typically available when disposing of all or part of your business. Cost estimates and volumes for BADR also include claims for Investors' Relief as the two reliefs cannot be separated in the data at present. Investors’ Relief claims make up only a very small proportion of the totals presented in the tables.
reliefs.notes: The figures presented include claims made by both individuals and trusts. A large increase in the cost of BADR is forecast for the 2024 to 2025 tax year to reflect taxpayers bringing forward BADR-eligible disposals from future years in anticipation of CGT tax rate increases. A related decrease in the cost of the relief is forecast for the 2025 to 2026 tax year as disposals that would have been realised in that year have been brought forward in time. The figures for 2019-20 onwards take into account the restriction of the relief lifetime limit for BADR from £10m to £1m, announced and implemented from 11 March 2020. Only eligible disposals made on or after 11 March 2020 are affected for the 2019-20 tax year whereas all eligible disposals are affected in consequent years which drives the decrease in the cost of the relief in those years.
reliefs.quality: Administrative data on the use of the relief, with significant further assumptions applied

reliefs.name: Investors' Relief
reliefs.description: Disposals chargeable to CGT of shares held in unlisted companies for a period of at least three years are charged at a rate of 10% subject to a lifetime limit of qualifying gains. The relief is not usually available if you or someone connected with you is an employee of the company. Cost estimates and claim volumes for Investors' Relief are included in the total for BADR (detailed on the row above) as the two reliefs cannot be separated in the data at present. Investors’ Relief claims make up only a very small proportion of the totals presented.
reliefs.notes: Cost estimates and claim volumes for Investors' Relief cannot be separated from those for Business Assets Disposal Relief (BADR), shown on the preceding row.
reliefs.quality: Administrative data on the use of the relief, with significant further assumptions applied

reliefs.name: High-End TV Tax Relief
reliefs.description: Television production companies can claim additional corporation tax relief on producing high-end TV programmes in the UK. Companies not making a profit may be able to surrender a loss in return for a tax credit. For expenditure incurred from 1 January 2024, companies were able to claim a new, ‘above-the-line’ tax credit, the Audio-Visual Expenditure Credit (AVEC). This will run in parallel with the existing HETV relief until HETV sunsets in April 2027, and will replace it from that date. Figures for 2024-25 include claims for AVEC made by TV production companies.

reliefs.name: Land remediation relief
reliefs.description: Corporation tax relief for land remediation expenditure incurred for the purposes of remedying contaminated or derelict land. The relief is an enhanced deduction from income of 150% of the qualifying land remediation expenditure. A company making a loss may surrender the loss to HMRC in return for a payable tax credit of 16% of the loss.

reliefs.name: Research and development tax relief: R&D Expenditure Credit
reliefs.description: Until 2024, this relief is mainly for larger companies, allowing companies to claim a taxable credit on their qualifying R&D expenditure. For accounting periods beginning on or after 1 April 2024, the RDEC scheme will become the merged RDEC scheme and will apply to all companies claiming R&D relief who do not satisfy the R&D intensity condition.
reliefs.quality: Administrative data on the use of the relief, with minimal further assumptions applied

reliefs.name: Research and development tax relief: small and medium companies scheme
reliefs.description: The SME scheme provides small and medium-sized companies with relief on R&D expenditure. Companies can claim an enhancement of 86% on their qualifying R&D expenditure against taxable profits. Loss-makers can surrender all or part of their losses attributable to R&D for a payable credit at a rate of 10% of the surrendered losses. Certain companies qualifying as R&D intensive (that is, their R&D expenditure is 40% or more of total expenditure) can surrender their losses for a 14.5% credit. These rates apply to expenditure incurred from 1 April 2023. Prior to this, the enhancement was 130% and the credit rate on surrenderable loss was 14.5% for all companies. For accounting periods starting on or after 1 April 2024, the relief for lossmaking, R&D intensive SMEs is referred to as ERIS and the intensity threshold is reduced to 30%. SMEs that do not pass the intensity condition or are profit-making will instead claim the merged RDEC scheme, which provides an ‘above the line’ credit of 20% on qualifying expenditure.
reliefs.quality: Administrative data on the use of the relief, with minimal further assumptions applied

reliefs.name: Relief for Freeport tax sites
reliefs.taxHead: NICs, Income Tax, Stamp Duty Land Tax and Corporation Tax
reliefs.description: The following reliefs are available in English Freeport tax sites: 1. A zero rate of Class 1 secondary NICs for eligible employees up to the freeports upper secondary threshold; 2. A 100% first-year allowance for expenditure by companies on certain new plant or machinery for use within Freeport tax sites. 3. An enhanced structures and buildings capital allowance providing relief for investment in qualifying construction costs of non-residential buildings or structures, and renovation or conversion costs of existing ones. 4. Relief from SDLT for purchases of non-residential land and property.
reliefs.notes: The outturn is estimated using HMRC’s Real Time Information, Corporation tax and SDLT tax returns. Freeports sites were designated later than expected resulting in a delay to the costs.

reliefs.name: Relief on employer National Insurance contributions for apprentices under 25

Costs are affected by changes to the number of apprentices under the age of 25, and changes to their wages between the Secondary Threshold and Apprentice Upper Secondary Threshold. The larger than usual increase in cost presented in the 2025-26 forecast is expected due to the employer NICs changes which came into effect in April 2025, namely the reduction of the secondary threshold from £9,100 to £5,000 and the increase of the employer NICs rate from 13.8% to 15%. As this is a relief for the employer, we report the number of employers claiming the relief.

reliefs.name: Annual Exempt Amount CGT

At Autumn Budget 2022 the Government announced that in 2023/24 those will be reduced to £6,000 for individuals and £3,000 for trusts and then again in 2024/25 to £3,000 for individuals and £1,500 for trusts.
reliefs.notes: The estimated cost of this exemption from capital gains tax does not represent the yield if this exemption were to be abolished, as consequential behavioural effects would substantially reduce yield.The cost in 2023-24 are estimates of the number of people benefitting from the AEA based on ONS data on wealth and HMRC self-assessment data. The change in nominal costs over time is largely due to changes in CGT outturn data. The large fall in the cost of relief between 2022-23 to 2023-24 is due to the AEA amount reducing from £12.3k to £6k in that year.
reliefs.quality: Administrative data on the use of the relief, with significant further assumptions applied.

reliefs.notes: D: Introduction of the relief is too recent for any data to be available.

Without this relief, a charge would apply to the entire income of offshore assets, where one or more of the investors are a UK resident. Therefore, costing this relief would be uninformative due to the scope of the assets that would come into charge.

reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Visiting forces, other than UK citizens
reliefs.description: Visiting forces and designated allied headquarters staff are treated as non-UK resident for CGT purposes. This complies with international agreements.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Redundancy payment
reliefs.description: Redundancy payments are disregarded for the purposes of calculating NIC liabilities.

reliefs.name: Employments disregarded
reliefs.description: Employment as a member of any international HQ or defence organisation designated under section 1 of the International HQ and Defence Organisations Act 1964 (there are certain exclusions).
reliefs.notes: N: We are reviewing what data is available, reason code to be allocated.

reliefs.name: Agency worker rules - excluded services
reliefs.description: Legislation does not apply to excluded services.
reliefs.notes: N: We are reviewing what data is available, reason code to be allocated.

reliefs.name: Clay, soil and other organic matter
reliefs.description: Aggregate consisting wholly of clay or soil or other organic matter is exempt from aggregates levy.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate which has previously been used for construction purposes (exempt by virtue of not being ‘taxable aggregate’)
reliefs.description: Aggregate which has previously been used for construction purposes is exempt from aggregates levy.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Production of lime or cement from limestone
reliefs.description: Any process for the production of lime or cement from limestone is exempt from aggregates levy.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Extracting industrial minerals
reliefs.description: Any process in which a relevant substance is extracted from any aggregate is exempt from aggregates levy (19 industrial minerals are listed).
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Shale not used for construction purposes
reliefs.description: Any use of shale which is not for construction purposes is exempt from aggregates levy
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate which is returned, unmixed, to the land at the site from which it was won (exempt by virtue of being not ‘commercially exploited')
reliefs.description: If a quantity of aggregate again becomes part of the land at the site from which it was won it is exempt from aggregates levy.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate used in an exempt process after the aggregates levy has been brought to account
reliefs.description: Tax credit against an aggregates levy may be available if an exempt process is applied to that aggregate.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate used in a prescribed industrial or agricultural process
reliefs.description: Tax credit against an aggregates levy may be available if any of it is used in a prescribed industrial or agricultural process (38 prescribed processes are listed).
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate disposed of without further processing to the originating site or a connected site
reliefs.description: Tax credit against an aggregates levy may be available where the aggregate is disposed of unprocessed to the originating site.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate which is sand or gravel and is used for beach replenishment
reliefs.description: Tax credit against an aggregates levy may be available where the aggregate is gravel or sand and is used for beach restoration purposes.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate disposed of to landfill
reliefs.description: Tax credit may be available against aggregates disposed of to landfill.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Aggregate won from a site and returned, unmixed, to a site occupied by the same person for agricultural or forestry purposes (exempt by virtue of being not ‘commercially exploited’)
reliefs.description: Where aggregate is won from any site and the same person also occupies another site for agricultural or forestry purposes, the aggregate will be exempt from aggregates levy if it is returned to the land, unmixed, on that other site.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Military flights
reliefs.description: Applies to an aircraft when its operation falls within certain exemptions set out in Annex I of EC Directive 2003/87 (EU ETS) which includes humanitarian flights, military, police, search and rescue and pilot training and Public Service Obligation flights.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Short Pleasure Flights
reliefs.description: Applies to flights that begin and end at the same airport and last less than 60 minutes. Includes pleasure flights and also flights undertaken for training and instruction.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Passengers travelling on connecting flights
reliefs.description: Passengers travelling on connecting flights are exempt from Air Passenger Duty. Avoids what could be seen as a double taxation agreement (DTA).
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Transit Passengers
reliefs.description: Transit Passengers are exempt from APD.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: (Other than self supplies) to various categories of electricity producers including combined heat and power (CHP) schemes
reliefs.description: Various categories of electricity producers.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Used to produce taxable commodities other than electricity
reliefs.description: Exemption for supplies to producers of commodities other than electricity (e.g. gas, coal, oils, uranium).
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Exemption for taxable commodities used to produce electricity in a generating station
reliefs.description: Exemption for taxable commodities used to produce electricity in a generating station other than a CHP, a small generating station or a stand-by generator.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Self-supplies of electricity by generators in specific circumstances
reliefs.description: Exemption from climate change levy for taxable commodities used by the producer (self supplies).
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Mining and quarrying waste
reliefs.description: A disposal is not a taxable disposal if it is naturally occurring material that is a by-product of commercial mining or quarrying operations.

reliefs.name: Backfilling of quarries
reliefs.description: A disposal is not a taxable disposal if it is qualifying material made at a quarry and meets certain conditions.

reliefs.name: Alcoholic Ingredients Relief
reliefs.description: Relief on the excise duty charged on the alcohol used in the production of eligible articles.
reliefs.notes: C: Information on the usage of this relief is available, but the cost is not quantifiable as it is dependent on other unknown factors.

reliefs.name: Subscriptions to trade unions, professional and other public interest bodies
reliefs.description: Exemption from VAT for subscriptions due to certain public interest bodies including trade unions and professional bodies.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Supplies of commercial property
reliefs.description: Exemption from VAT for supplies of commercial and residential land and property.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Investment gold
reliefs.description: Exemption from VAT for supplies of investment gold or certain rights over investment gold.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Postal services
reliefs.description: Exemption from VAT for the provision of certain postal services by the Royal Mail.
reliefs.notes: E: Exemption under the Freedom of Information Act, such as Data Protection.

reliefs.name: Supplies of goods where input tax cannot be recovered
reliefs.description: Exemption from VAT on goods supplied where certain input tax cannot be recovered.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: International services
reliefs.description: Zero rating applies to work on goods acquired or temporarily imported into the UK and destined for subsequent export.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

reliefs.name: Tax-free shops
reliefs.description: Zero rating of supplies made at tax free shops made to individuals leaving the UK for a destination outside the EC.
reliefs.notes: A: Information on the usage of this relief is not required in tax returns and cannot be reliably estimated from other data sources, and the cost of collection for statistical purposes is disproportionate.

commentary.whyChanged: HMRC attributes the recent increase in estimated ISA relief to higher interest rates and lower dividend and capital-gains allowances. Accumulation of assets inside ISAs explains the longer-run rise.
commentary.distribution: Holdings are larger on average among older and higher-income ISA holders. These are holdings distributions, not a direct allocation of tax relief by beneficiary.

notes: Subscriptions are annual flows; market values are accumulated stocks, including investment returns. Neither is the fiscal cost of ISA relief.
Accounts subscribed to are not unique individual holders. Individuals may subscribe to more than one type of ISA.
Holder estimates combine a sample of individual returns with provider aggregates; calibration can change reported holder counts.
Distributional information is for 2022-23; aggregate subscriptions and holdings extend to 2023-24. Do not imply that these observations describe the same year.
Lifetime ISA assets are already included in cash and stocks-and-shares market values. Insurance components are of-which rows and are excluded from component totals here.
Income and age distributions describe ISA assets only, not total household wealth or revenue obtainable from reform.
Rounding means component counts may not exactly sum to published totals.
July 2026 pension statistics are a later vintage than the January 2026 tax-relief headline. Do not splice the two vintages.
Gross pension relief, net pension relief and tax collected on pensions are different measures; table totals overlap their component rows.
